item.title: Kakunodate Samurai District & Cherry Blossoms — Akita Guide
item.description: Kakunodate is one of Japan’s best-preserved samurai towns — a 400-year-old bukeyashiki (samurai residence) street lined with black-walled mansions and weeping cherry trees planted by samurai families. Six original residences are open to the public, and in late April the shidarezakura drape over the walls like pink waterfalls, one of Tohoku’s finest hanami. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Kakunodate, Senboku, Akita Hours Street always open; residences ~9:00–17:00 Admission Some residences ~¥400 Time needed 1.
